questions_for_integrator: Does the s-bend line loss sit at the same progress point as in iterations 0 and 7 (late sensing on the tightest bend), or has it moved?
Does the oval gain at y 0.06 m hold with the same controller, and does steering_oscillation stay below about 0.2?
Would an intermediate offset of y 0.055 m likely keep most of the oval gain while recovering s-bend progress toward 0.148? Please say if you see a reason it would not.

intent: Keep the best-scoring geometry (five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.06 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, body unchanged). Expect the oval gain from iteration 9 to hold, and expect the s-bend shortfall to persist at about 0.14 progress. Ask for per-track telemetry on where the single loss occurs, so the next iteration can decide whether to try an intermediate offset of y 0.055 m.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that the forward offset trades oval progress against s-bend progress. Y 0.06 m gave the best total score but fell below the s-bend baseline. Iteration 10 holds the design fixed so the per-track loss point can be read. If the s-bend loss is at a late-sensing point, the next geometry test is y 0.055 m. If the Integrator reports lag-driven oscillation, the forward offset is at its useful limit and the remaining lever is the controller.
rationale:
Iteration 9 is the best result so far at 52.985, against 52.28 for the baseline. Moving the five 12 mm sensors forward from y 0.05 to y 0.06 m raised oval progress from 0.138 to 0.151, and oval score rose from 56.25 to 62.77. S-bend progress fell from 0.148 to 0.140, and s-bend score fell from 61.01 to 57.74. Slalom was unchanged in progress (0.097) and its loss stayed at 2.0. Line loss stayed at 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend, and steering oscillation stayed low (0.10 and 0.14), so the robot is not jittering and the loss is still a single dropout at a fixed point.

The Integrator's rule (2) says to return to y 0.05 m if s-bend progress falls below baseline with line loss at 1.0. The rule was written to protect the baseline, but the objective is the race score, and the net result improved. The oval gain (about +6.5 points) outweighs the s-bend loss (about -3.3). The change is therefore a trade-off, not a clear regression. I keep y 0.06 m for this race because it is the best measured design. I do not interpolate to y 0.055 m in this iteration, because an untested offset could lose the gain. The s-bend shortfall suggests the forward lead helps the open oval but gives late sensing on tight bends. Wheel radius, track, mass, footprint and span stay at baseline, so the result can be attributed to the offset alone.

Expected result: about 52.9 to 53.0, with oval progress near 0.15, s-bend near 0.14, and line loss still 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend and 2.0 on slalom.
